chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all together from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Will you not inform me from where you knew and ruled that the wiping is [limited] to part of the head and part of the two feet? He laughed and then said: … Then he said: 'Allah intends not to place upon you any difficulty' and 'difficulty' is 'discomfort/constriction'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for limiting the wiping of the head and feet in ablution?
ai.summary: Zurara queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the jurisprudential basis for limiting ablution wiping to a portion of the head and feet. The Imam responds by citing the verse 'Allah intends not to place upon you any difficulty' (5:6), interpreting 'haraj' as 'dhiq' (narrowness or discomfort) to argue that requiring full wiping would impose undue hardship, thereby establishing a principle of ease in ritual practice.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father AND Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan all together from Hammad b. Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abi Ja’far عليه السلام: will you not inform me how you knew and ruled that the wiping should only be limited to a part of the head and a part of the feet, so he laughed and then said: … then he said: “Allāh does not intend to place upon you [in the religion] any difficulty” [5:6] – and “difficulty” is “discomfort”.
